comparable_cases.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization for a bar within a full-service restaurant at 970–974 Valencia St, only 66 m away in NCT-Valencia zoning—the same district and block as the subject property. Direct precedent for bar use approval.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This use decision was withdrawn in January 2011 after filing in August 2010. The withdrawal of a bar CUA in NCT-Valencia on the same block signals that bar approvals in this corridor are not automatic; applicants may face hurdles that lead them to abandon the process.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral (Planning approval) for a Place of Entertainment permit at 998 Valencia St, only 52 m away in NCT-Valencia. Approved in 2014 as accessory to an existing retail use, with the entertainment area limited to 1/3 of gross floor area.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved live entertainment accessory to retail under Planning Code § 703.2(b)(1)(C)(viii). This is an agency referral for an Entertainment Commission permit, not a use decision, and the entertainment was limited to 1/3 of the floor area—not a primary bar use. Shows that live entertainment as an accessory can be approved, but does not establish bar-use precedent.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral approving continuation of an existing Type 41 license at 1007–1017 Valencia St, 45 m away in NCT-Valencia, decided January 2008. Approval expressly stated it does not establish a new bar use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved continuation of a Type 41 eating-place license but explicitly noted the approval does not establish a new bar use at the location. This reinforces that a Type 41 (restaurant) and Type 42 (bar) are treated differently under Planning Code § 102, and that converting from one to the other is a change of use requiring CUA.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral (Board of Supervisors liquor-license PCN referral) at 2519 Mission St, 210 m away in NCT-Mission. Planning recommended approval for a nonprofit theater with an accessory bar use in July 2021.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning recommended approval of a Public Convenience or Necessity finding for an accessory bar within a nonprofit theater, not a stand-alone bar. The decision was an agency referral (PCN recommendation), not a Commission hearing on a CUA, so it signals Planning's willingness to support accessory alcohol service in an arts context but does not predict CUA outcomes for primary bar uses.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral for Entertainment Commission Place of Entertainment and Extended Hours Premises permits at 2500 Mission St, 145 m away in NCT-Mission, approved July 2026. Addresses live entertainment and late-night operation in the Mission corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved an Entertainment Commission referral for a POE + Extended Hours permit in NCT-Mission two blocks away in mid-2026, demonstrating that live entertainment and extended hours are feasible on this corridor. This is an agency referral (Planning says the zoning allows the EC permit), not a use-decision CUA, so it confirms permitting pathway but not Planning Commission approval standar…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral approving a Place of Entertainment permit for restaurant and nighttime entertainment uses (Arcana) at 2512 Mission St, 152 m away in NCT-Mission, decided November 2020.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved live entertainment (POE permit) for a restaurant + nighttime entertainment use in NCT-Mission in 2020. This is an agency referral showing zoning compliance for a POE, not a discretionary CUA for a bar, but it confirms that live entertainment paired with food service is routinely approved on Mission Street.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization for a change of use from retail to a bona fide eating place with Type 41 license and live entertainment at 2519 Mission St, 210 m away in NCT-Mission. Filed July 2019, withdrawn October 2019.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A CUA for a Type 41 eating place with live entertainment was withdrawn after three months in NCT-Mission. The withdrawal of a restaurant + entertainment CUA (not even a bar use) suggests applicants may encounter process delays, regulatory conditions, or feasibility concerns that lead them to pull applications in the Mission SUD even for less-intensive uses.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral for a Limited Live Performance permit accessory to a retail store (Lost Weekend Video) at 1034 Valencia St, 94 m away in NCT-Valencia. Denied April 2015.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning denied a Limited Live Performance permit for live music accessory to a video store in NCT-Valencia in 2015. This is an agency referral denial (not a CUA), and the record does not state why. The denial of even a limited entertainment permit flags that accessory live entertainment is not automatically approved, though this case predates current Entertainment Commission LLP rules.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization approved December 1999 for an outdoor activity area in conjunction with a full-service restaurant/bar at 2526–2548 Mission St (Foreign Cinema), 159 m away in NCT-Mission.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning Commission approved a CUA for a restaurant/bar with outdoor seating in NCT-Mission in 1999. This is a use decision (CUA) that was approved, showing the Commission has historically approved full-service restaurant/bar combinations in the Mission corridor, though the record predates the Mission Alcohol SUD overlay (enacted 2008) that now restricts new bar licenses.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization approved July 2007 to change from a bar use to retail (AT&T store) at 2410–2412 Mission St, 193 m away in NCT-Mission. Demonstrates that bar-to-retail conversions are approved.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning Commission approved a CUA to convert a bar to retail in NCT-Mission in 2007, one year before the Mission Alcohol SUD was enacted. The approval of a bar-to-retail change confirms that eliminating a bar use is encouraged, but it does not provide precedent for creating a new bar use under the current SUD restrictions.

filing_playbook.action: Request a written determination from SF Planning confirming whether Planning Code § 249.60 permits a license transferred from outside the Mission SUD or requires an intra-SUD transfer.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a letter to the Planning Department's Zoning Administrator citing Planning Code § 249.60 and describing the concept as a wine bar seeking to transfer an ABC license. Ask whether the SUD's intra-district transfer rule applies. Request a written Zoning Determination or interpretation before filing the CUA. If the answer is that only intra-SUD transfers are allowed, identify available licenses within the SUD through an ABC license broker before proceeding.

filing_playbook.action: File the building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements and change of use, routed through Planning, DPH, SFFD, and PUC.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit stamped architectural, mechanical, plumbing, and electrical plans showing the bar build-out, kitchen equipment, hood and suppression system, ADA restrooms, and finishes. Mark the application as a change of use from restaurant to bar. Route the permit to Planning, DPH, SFFD, and PUC (grease interceptor). Pay the plan-check and permit fees (percentage of construction valuation, typically $800–$15,000). Electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits are pulled by licensed subcontractors. Allow 2–4 months for full interdepartmental review.

filing_playbook.action: File the health permit to operate application and schedule the pre-opening DPH inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the health permit application online with the Business Account Number, Location ID, EIN, DPH plan-check approval, and food safety manager certificate. Pay the $470 permit fee (FY 2026–27). Schedule the final inspection with the assigned inspector. Walk the space against the DPH checklist (hand sinks, hot water, sealed surfaces) one week before the inspection. You cannot serve the public before it is issued.

timeline_cost.notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per the catalog), followed by the ABC Type 42 license (60–150 days, or 90–240 days if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding or protest adds time), and the Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days). The building permit with change of use runs in parallel after CUA approval (14–120 days for plan review). Minimum timeline assumes an uncontested CUA decided in 4 months, an unprotested ABC application in 2 months, and a POE permit in 1.5 months, totaling roughly 7 months. Maximum timeline assumes a CUA with one continuance (10 months), ABC with PCN referral and protest (8 months), and a contested POE hearing (4 months), totaling 18+ months if stages are sequential. The $3,100 CUA base fee, $2,708 POE fee, $1,000–$1,600 ABC fee, $828–$2,207 DPH plan check, $470 health permit, and $800–$15,000 building permit sum to roughly $8,500–$35,000 in government fees (construction cost determines the building permit fee). If an intra-SUD Type 42 license must be purchased from another bar, add $50,000–$150,000 (estimated, as Type 42 market prices in the Mission SUD are not published) and 90–180 days for escrow and transfer, making the true minimum timeline 12–15 months and total upfront cost $60,000–$185,000.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St sits inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District in the NCT-Valencia zone, where a bar is a conditional use that requires a Conditional Use Authorization. The records show an active Type 41 (beer-and-wine eating place) license issued November 2023 to Sarita's Grill & Beer, establishing the space as a restaurant; converting to a wine bar (ABC Type 42, a bar use under Planning Code § 102) is a change of use. The Mission SUD requires any new bar to use a license transferred from another bar *within the SUD*—buying a Type 42 from outside the district is prohibited. The block is extremely active: 24 food/drink businesses and 9 ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft, triggering ABC's undue-concentration flag; 51 on-sale licenses within 1,000 ft. Few comparable bar decisions have been filed nearby in recent years (only 3 dated use decisions in 10 years, too few for a reliable approval rate), though one entertainment permit was approved across the street at 998 Valencia and a Place of Entertainment + Extended Hours venue opened recently at 2500 Mission.
